questions.question: What happens after the first True branch in an if-elif-else chain executes?
options: Python skips the remaining elif and else blocks immediately
Python continues to check every subsequent elif condition
Python restarts from the top of the chain
questions.correct_answer: Python skips the remaining elif and else blocks immediately
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! Only the first matching branch executes in an if-elif ladder.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Python immediately exits the chain after executing the first matching branch.

questions.question: When is an 'else' block executed in an if-elif-else ladder?
options: Only when all previous if and elif conditions evaluate to False
Whenever the last elif is True
At the start of every iteration
questions.correct_answer: Only when all previous if and elif conditions evaluate to False
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! 'else' is the ultimate catch-all when no conditions match.
questions.explanation_incorrect: else runs only if every preceding condition was False.

questions.question: If score = 95, why would placing 'if score >= 50:' above 'elif score >= 90:' be a bug?
options: Because 95 >= 50 is True, so it will print Grade C and never reach Grade A
Because Python raises a SyntaxError if numbers are in ascending order
questions.correct_answer: Because 95 >= 50 is True, so it will print Grade C and never reach Grade A
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! Broad checks shadow more specific checks if placed first.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Since 95 >= 50 is True first, Grade C would execute and Grade A would be unreachable.

questions.question: Can you have multiple 'elif' statements inside a single conditional block?
options: Yes, as many as needed between if and else
No, maximum of one elif allowed
Only if each elif checks different variables
questions.correct_answer: Yes, as many as needed between if and else
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! You can chain as many elif statements as your logic requires.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Python allows chaining unlimited elif statements between if and else.
